terms.grammar: conjunction, with the moods of sī: indicative for a real case, subjunctive for a supposed one
evidence: Cic. Amic. 104: omnia autem brevia tolerābilia esse dēbent, etiamsī magna sunt
terms.comment: The main clause often has tamen. Plain et sī or sī … tamen says the same.

terms.grammar: conjunction, with the moods of sī
terms.comment: The same word as etiamsī, but in classical prose mostly of a fact, “although” (see that record).

evidence: Ov. Pont. 3.4.79: ut dēsint vīrēs, tamen est laudanda voluntās (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Concessive ut: “suppose that”, answered by tamen.

evidence: Ov. Rem. 213–214: tū tantum quamvīs firmīs retinēbere vinclīs, ī procul

phrases.latin: omnia autem brevia tolerābilia esse dēbent, etiamsī magna sunt
phrases.english: and everything short ought to be bearable, even if it is great

phrases.latin: quīcumque turpī fraude semel innōtuit, etiam sī vērum dīcit, āmittit fidem
phrases.english: whoever has once been known for a shameful lie loses trust even if he tells the truth

phrases.latin: nūllus sūmptus est, et sī sūmptus esset, tamen valētūdinis causā experīrēs
phrases.english: it costs nothing, and even if it did cost something, you would still try it for your health

phrases.latin: ut dēsint vīrēs, tamen est laudanda voluntās
phrases.english: even if the strength is lacking, the will deserves praise

phrases.latin: tū tantum quamvīs firmīs retinēbere vinclīs, ī procul, et longās carpere perge viās
phrases.english: only, even if strong ties hold you back, go far away, and set out on long roads

Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-cicero-philosophica, loci-phaedrus, loci-cato, loci-ovidius), checked against the editions named there.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
